verses.1: Happy those who do not follow the counsel of the wicked, Nor go the way of sinners, nor sit in company with scoffers.
verses.2: Rather, the law of the LORD is their joy; God's law they study day and night.
verses.3: They are like a tree planted near streams of water, that yields its fruit in season; Its leaves never wither; whatever they do prospers.
verses.4: But not the wicked! They are like chaff driven by the wind.
verses.5: Therefore the wicked will not survive judgment, nor will sinners in the assembly of the just.
verses.6: The LORD watches over the way of the just, but the way of the wicked leads to ruin. [Psalm 1] A preface to the whole Book of Psalms, contrasting with striking similes the destiny of the good and the wicked. The psalm views life as activity, as choosing either the good or the bad. Each "way" brings its inevitable consequences. The wise through their good actions will experience rootedness and life, and the wicked, rootlessness and death. Those: literally, "the man." That word is used here and in many of the Psalms as typical, and therefore is translated "they." The way: a common biblical term for manner of living or moral conduct ( ⇒ Psalm 32:8; ⇒ 101:2, 6; ⇒ Proverb 2:20; ⇒ 1 Kings 8:36). The law of the LORD: either the Torah, the first five books of the Bible, or, more probably, divine teaching or instruction. The wicked: those who by their actions distance themselves from God's life-giving presence. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.128: For the leader. Of David. In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to me, "Flee like a bird to the mountains!
verses.129: See how the wicked string their bows, fit their arrows to the string to shoot from the shadows at the upright.
verses.130: When foundations are being destroyed, what can the upright do?"
verses.131: The LORD is in his holy temple; the LORD'S throne is in heaven. God's eyes keep careful watch; they test all peoples.
verses.132: The LORD tests the good and the bad, hates those who love violence,
verses.133: And rains upon the wicked fiery coals and brimstone, a scorching wind their allotted cup.
verses.134: The LORD is just and loves just deeds; the upright shall see his face. [Psalm 11] A song of trust. Though friends counsel flight to the mountain country (a traditional hideout) to escape trouble ( ⇒ Psalm 11:1-3), the innocent psalmist reaffirms confidence in God, who protects those who seek asylum in the temple ( ⇒ Psalm 11:4-7). Foundations: usually understood of public order. Cf ⇒ Psalm 82:5. Their allotted cup: the cup that God gives people to drink is a common figure for their destiny. Cf ⇒ Psalm 16:5; ⇒ 75:9; ⇒ Matthew 20:22; ⇒ 26:39; ⇒ Rev 14:10. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
